ao_demand_evidence.new_input: Suggest why a muscle must consume glucose faster if its energy supply shifts from aerobic to anaerobic respiration but its energy demand stays unchanged.
ao_demand_evidence.inference: Anaerobic respiration releases much less energy from each glucose molecule. More glucose must therefore be broken down each minute to supply the same energy.
ao_demand_evidence.classification: reasoning from the supplied case, rather than a renamed recall prompt.

ao_demand_evidence.new_input: Explain the likely bend of a young shoot when a treatment makes its left side elongate 4 mm and its right side elongate 1 mm during the same period.
ao_demand_evidence.inference: It bends towards the right. The left side grows 3 mm more, so it becomes the longer outside of the curve.
ao_demand_evidence.classification: reasoning from the supplied case, rather than a renamed recall prompt.

ao_demand_evidence.new_input: Explain why the second neurone stops responding when impulses still reach the end of the first neurone but a chemical stops neurotransmitter being released. The receptors are not affected.
ao_demand_evidence.inference: The impulse is electrical and cannot cross the gap without neurotransmitter. With no transmitter binding, the receptors on the second neurone are not stimulated, so it does not respond.
ao_demand_evidence.classification: reasoning from the supplied case, rather than a renamed recall prompt.

ao_demand_evidence.new_input: Explain why a pupil cannot narrow in bright light if the circular muscles of the iris cannot contract, although the radial muscles relax normally.
ao_demand_evidence.inference: The pupil narrows only when the circular muscles contract. Relaxing the radial muscles alone does not pull the pupil smaller, so it stays wide.
ao_demand_evidence.classification: reasoning from the supplied case, rather than a renamed recall prompt.

ao_demand_evidence.new_input: Explain why an older person whose lens has become stiff cannot focus on a near object, even though the ciliary muscles contract and the suspensory ligaments slacken.
ao_demand_evidence.inference: A stiff lens cannot become thicker and more curved, so it cannot refract light more. The near object is therefore not focused on the retina.
ao_demand_evidence.classification: reasoning from the supplied case, rather than a renamed recall prompt.

ao_demand_evidence.new_input: Explain why an eye cannot focus on a distant object if its suspensory ligaments are damaged and cannot pull on the lens, even though the ciliary muscles relax.
ao_demand_evidence.inference: The lens is not pulled thinner and flatter. It stays thick, so it refracts light too strongly and the distant object is not focused on the retina.
ao_demand_evidence.classification: reasoning from the supplied case, rather than a renamed recall prompt.

ao_demand_evidence.new_input: Suggest which control system best fits each observation: response X begins almost immediately after a skin stimulus and ends quickly; response Y follows a blood-borne signal and persists for hours.
ao_demand_evidence.inference: X fits nervous control because it is rapid and brief. Y fits hormonal control because the signal travels in blood and its effect lasts a long time.
ao_demand_evidence.classification: reasoning from the supplied case, rather than a renamed recall prompt.

ao_demand_evidence.new_input: Explain which culture is directly affected by medicine K: K blocks bacterial cell-wall formation; culture A contains susceptible bacteria and culture B contains viruses inside animal cells.
ao_demand_evidence.inference: K affects culture A, because its bacteria make cell walls and K blocks this. The viruses in culture B have no bacterial cell wall, so K does not affect them.
ao_demand_evidence.classification: reasoning from the supplied case, rather than a renamed recall prompt.

ao_demand_evidence.new_input: Explain why route X presents a greater blood-borne infection risk than route Y: X reuses a syringe containing another person’s blood; Y uses new sterile equipment with no shared preparation equipment.
ao_demand_evidence.inference: X can inject another person’s infected blood directly into the next user. Y uses new sterile equipment, so there is no blood from another person to carry the virus.
ao_demand_evidence.classification: reasoning from the supplied case, rather than a renamed recall prompt.

ao_demand_evidence.new_input: Suggest why, when adrenaline is released in a person whose liver glycogen store has been used up, the pulse rate rises but blood glucose does not.
ao_demand_evidence.inference: Adrenaline acts on the heart, so the pulse rate still rises. Adrenaline raises blood glucose by causing the liver to break down glycogen; with the store used up there is no glycogen to convert, so blood glucose does not rise.
ao_demand_evidence.classification: reasoning from the supplied case, rather than a renamed recall prompt.

ao_demand_evidence.new_input: Explain why a heating controller that switches on extra heating whenever a room becomes too warm, and still more heating as the temperature rises, is not an example of negative feedback.
ao_demand_evidence.inference: Its response adds to the temperature rise instead of opposing it. The temperature therefore moves further from the set level and is not brought back to normal.
ao_demand_evidence.classification: reasoning from the supplied case, rather than a renamed recall prompt.
